description: Delyth Associates is a multidisciplinary team of engineering students combining technology, design, AI, and problem-solving to develop innovative solutions for real-world Earth and space challenges.
summary:
Spacecraft fire safety is a life-critical constraint for deep-space exploration, yet terrestrial flammability standards cannot predict microgravity combustion. To solve this, we developed PYRO-ASTRA, an authoritative operational fire-safety intelligence engine and 3D combustion laboratory powered by NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository.

PYRO-ASTRA synthesizes 1,815 authentic flight test runs across 18 NASA microgravity investigations (including BASS-II, FLEX, SAFFIRE, Flame Design, and SAME). Unlike conventional generative AI that hallucinates unmeasured values, PYRO-ASTRA enforces strict non-negotiable scientific governance: every data point carries provenance, missing values are preserved as null ("not reported"), burner-feed oxidizer (85%O2) is strictly isolated from cabin air, and zero partial-gravity extrapolations are permitted.

The platform features interactive environment ranking for Artemis and Gateway atmospheres, a continuous GLSL volumetric 3D combustion simulator demonstrating Burke-Schumann flame sheets, and Ask ASTRA a grounded AI safety analyst protected by a deterministic post-inference verifier. PYRO-ASTRA bridges the gap between raw flight telemetry and operational habitat safety de
details:
PYRO-ASTRA is an evidence dashboard for crewed-habitat fire safety built on the NASA PSI public record. It ingests 1,815 experimental-table rows (1,807 test runs plus 8 candidate condition sets) from 18 investigations: solid fuels (BASS, BASS-II, SAFFIRE-I/II/III), liquid droplets (FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI), gas flames (Flame Design, ACME BRE/E-FIELD/s-Flame, SLICE, Spice, CFI-G), smoke (SAME, SAME-R) and dust (DAFT). Every number links to its source file, row and column. The dashboard ranks investigations by relevance to a chosen atmosphere (ISS 21% O₂, the planned lunar habitat 34% O₂ / 8.2 psi, spacesuit), compares stated and table-listed values, shows reported ranges and gaps, offers a dataset for modeling, and answers questions through Ask ASTRA. Ask is deterministic by default, with an optional AI mode (Groq) whose every answer is checked by a verifier.

It shows where the public record has no data. Across the table rows that report both oxygen and pressure, none combine cabin O₂ ≥ 30% with pressure ≤ 10.2 psi, and the record has no partial-gravity combustion data. Instead of guessing, the dashboard marks the gaps and shows the nearest measured conditions. It also gives researchers a standardized, machine-readable dataset (1,815 rows, per-row provenance, SHA-256 checksums, field dictionary) that supports predictive modeling by others, with a demonstration model that refuses to answer outside its measured range.

It treats a gap in the data as the result. The empty region at the lunar-habitat atmosphere is the headline. AI reads and drafts, while code verifies every number, unit and fuel, and a rule-based layer refuses partial-gravity predictions, propellant questions, and confusion of burner oxidizer with cabin air. The same refusal logic gates the demonstration model.

Provenance first: nulls instead of guesses, no unit conversion unless the source states the unit, and burner/oxidizer-stream oxygen kept separate from cabin air. Different fuel phases are never combined. Ranges are labelled as envelopes of reported ranges, not confirmed test combinations. Where metadata and tables disagree, both are shown. AI is disclosed, rate-limited and optional, with an offline default.

A 3D Combustion Lab renders an illustrative flame visualization (Three.js/WebGL) controlled by reported conditions such as oxygen, pressure and flow. It is an explanatory visualization, not measured data or a prediction. A Beginner/Advanced mode switches between plain-language explanations and full technical detail with provenance.”

Tools, languages, hardware, software
TypeScript, Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Python (ingestion and analysis), Groq API (qwen/qwen3.8-27b, optional), Vercel for hosting. No special hardware.
